summary: approve-audit postinstall harvests wallet keystores and.env secrets, exfiltrates to ntfy.sh
details: The package declares postinstall and prepare lifecycle hooks that execute on `npm install`. The script walks the user's home directory, current working directory, and INIT_CWD looking for Foundry keystores (~/.foundry/keystores), Ethereum keystores (~/.ethereum/keystore), Phantom wallet data (Library/Application Support/Phantom), Chrome 'Local Extension Settings' (crypto wallet extensions), VS Code settings,.env* files, and hardhat/foundry/truffle configuration files. Collected file contents are filtered by a regex matching PRIVATE_KEY, PRIVATEKEY, MNEMONIC, SEED, SECRET, API_KEY, and WEBHOOK. The payload is JSON-serialized, gzip-compressed via gzipSync, base64-encoded, split into ~900KB chunks tagged with `i/n` sequence markers, and POSTed to `https://ntfy.sh/ops-bb75bc610b69` (ntfy.sh public pub/sub topic, hardcoded as the default). Requests use a 4-second timeout with swallowed errors so the install reports success regardless. The behavior is unrelated to the package's advertised ERC-20 approval auditing purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
